title: Consumer value pressure is being expressed through scale-versus-value retailer choice
source_unit: Coresight Research, Consumers Reward Scale as Amazon Gains: US Consumer Survey Insights, September 29, 2026 public report preview
geography: United States; consumer sentiment and retailer/category shopping tracked weekly and described by income group

observations.period: September 29, 2026 public preview; current report scope

denominator.unit: publicly described Coresight US Consumer Survey Insights report

sentiment_segmentation.value: the report examines consumer sentiment in total and by income, weekly

retailer_choice.value: the public title frames consumers as rewarding scale while Amazon gains and dollar stores lose shopper momentum

mechanism.value: Macroeconomic pressure can be translated into retailer selection, with household income shaping whether scale, value, convenience or assortment is experienced as the safer purchase route

observations.method: Public preview of a Coresight Research deep-dive based on weekly US consumer survey data; the preview identifies the measures and headline but does not expose the full report or underlying tables.
observations.uncertainty: The public preview does not provide sample size, field dates, weighting, subgroup estimates, retailer shares, effect sizes, causal evidence or the full definition of scale, value or shopper momentum.
observations.subgroup: U.S. consumers segmented by income, retailer visited and selected purchase categories; detailed subgroup composition is not publicly shown in the preview.
observations.counterinterpretation: A retailer's shopper momentum may reflect assortment, promotion, geography, delivery, product mix or survey timing rather than a durable income-driven shift toward scale.

observations.period: September 2026; weekly consumer sentiment, retailer shopping and category purchase behavior

tracked_outcomes.value: the report includes weekly rates of shopping at major retailers and weekly rates of purchasing in selected retail categories

economic_context.value: the public preview positions the analysis against shifting economic conditions, inflationary pressures and the Iran conflict

mechanism.value: Consumer sentiment and observed shopping routes should be read together: confidence can diverge from where households actually shop and what categories they continue to purchase

observations.method: Coresight public description of a weekly US consumer survey databank and related deep-dive report.
observations.uncertainty: The preview does not reveal whether sentiment changes precede shopping changes, how purchases are measured, or whether retailer movement reflects substitution, frequency, basket size or new shoppers.
observations.subgroup: Households with different incomes, shopping channels, retail preferences and category exposures.
observations.counterinterpretation: Weekly movement can be seasonal or promotional and need not represent a durable change in household welfare, retailer power or consumer loyalty.

observations.period: Public preview boundary; access and interpretation

access_condition.value: the page exposes the research questions and data categories but requires subscription or purchase for the full report

open_question.value: The public evidence supports a hypothesis about scale, value and income-divergent retailer choice, but not a quantified estimate of who switched, why or with what household consequences

next_test.value: The next test is to connect retailer choice to price, basket composition, delivery access, travel time, promotions, credit, brand trust and realized household room

observations.method: Direct review of the public Coresight report preview and its linked description of the underlying weekly survey databank.
observations.uncertainty: Full report access is unavailable in the public preview, so no numerical retailer comparison or causal claim is made here.
observations.subgroup: Consumers and retailers whose choices and market power are shaped by income, geography, price pressure, scale and value positioning.
observations.counterinterpretation: The public headline may reflect a short-period commercial signal rather than an enduring cultural or consumer transformation.
